sources.entry: Software development is the process of conceiving, specifying, designing, programming, documenting, testing, and bug fixing involved in creating and maintaining applications, frameworks, or other software components.

summary.name: Software development (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing the process of designing, creating, testing, and maintaining software, including methodologies, life cycle phases, and common tools.
use_cases: learning the phases of a software project
understanding roles in a software team
choosing between waterfall and iterative approaches
summary.what_it_does: The article defines software development as designing, creating, testing, and maintaining software, and places it within software engineering. It compares methodologies such as code-and-fix, waterfall, agile (with Scrum and extreme programming as derivatives), and DevOps. It walks through the life cycle phases: feasibility, analysis, design, programming, testing, and production. It also covers documentation, effort estimation, IDEs, version control, and intellectual property issues with open-source licenses.
notable: Compares development methodologies from code-and-fix to waterfall, agile, and DevOps
Covers the full software development life cycle phase by phase
Includes a 2009 estimate that 32% of software projects were delivered on time, on budget, and with full functionality
caveats: Encyclopedic overview rather than a tool or hands-on guide
Some cited statistics and tool-estimation claims are dated (e.g., 2009, 2019)
